title: Undetected low-degree coefficients vanish
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let the target be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $J$ and $P$ be coordinate sets. Fix signs on $P$, let $k$ be a natural number, and let the failure parameter lie strictly between $0$ and $1/2$. Suppose $|J|\le k$ and the target depends only on coordinates in $J$. For a batch of the prescribed finite number of examples on the coordinates outside $P$, assume that every estimated Fourier coefficient in the low-degree family for the resulting restricted target differs from its true coefficient by less than the prescribed accuracy, and that the procedure for detecting a nonempty frequency returns none. Then every nonempty coordinate set $S$ of size at most $\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor$ has zero Fourier coefficient for that restricted target, viewed as real-valued.
